What's new in 2.30.0

The menu shows every tool at once, Agent Watch can tell your sessions apart, and the images you feed the tools are kept where you can find them again.

The menu bar shows everything

  • Every tool on one screenful. Three columns instead of one long scrolling list — you open a menu to find something, and a list you have to scroll can't be scanned. Nothing is a gesture away any more.
  • It fits your screen. On a narrower display it drops to two columns, or one, and grows taller instead of running off the edge.
  • Signed out, it asks you to sign in rather than listing twenty-two tools that can't run until you have.

Agent Watch ⌃⌥M

  • Every session gets its own character. Two agents in one repo used to draw the same animal; now no two sessions on screen are ever alike, and sessions sharing a folder are numbered — Dax 1, Dax 2 — on the corner of their avatar and in their name.
  • Only what's actually running. Close a terminal and its session leaves the list within seconds. Dax looks for the agent process itself now, instead of trusting a file that outlives the session that wrote it.
  • Status at a glance. A green light for working, yellow for a session that needs you, grey for one at rest — with the state in words and how long it's been that way counting up beside it. A resting session's animal stands still.
  • It brings up the right terminal. Selecting a session raises the tab actually running it, even when two sessions share a folder.

Dax Shots

  • The images you use are kept. Image to URL, Image Ask, Image to Prompt and Image to Text now save every picture you hand them to ~/Pictures/Dax Shots, one folder per tool, named the way macOS names screenshots. These tools give you back a link or an answer; the picture itself used to be nowhere you could go and look for it.

Clipboard History ⌃⌥C

  • A quiet signal instead of a chime. The menu bar icon becomes a downward arrow for a moment when something is copied. The sound is off by default now — turn it back on in Settings if you liked it.

Signing up

  • The photo is its own step, and you can skip it. It used to sit above the name and email fields, where the one optional thing on the screen looked like one of the required ones.
  • The welcome screen lets go by itself. A short countdown instead of a Continue button, with your photo on it if you set one.

Also in this release

  • Open Project remembers the agent you picked. Choosing Claude Code — YOLO used to quietly revert to plain Claude Code next time.
  • Long toasts fit. Results from AI Text Transform, Image to Text and Context Fill were spilling out of the card instead of growing to hold the text.
  • The version number sits at the foot of Settings and opens the changelog.
  • Bring-your-own-key isn't being offered while we work on it. Anyone already using their own key is unaffected.
  • Signed, notarized, universal (Apple Silicon & Intel), macOS 14+.
